title: observability-drift-detection-dashboard-versioning-for-private-installs
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Private installs have been drifting from the upstream observability configuration over time (dashboard edits, alert fingerprint changes, and Helm values drift). This PR adds automated drift detection for Prometheus/Grafana manifests and an opinionated dashboard versioning and rollback path integrated into the installer tooling. Goals: 1) Detect when cluster-side observability resources differ from the last-applied installer state; 2) Capture and version dashboards and alert rules as part of release artifacts; 3) Provide a safe rollback path that can reapply the last-known-good dashboard set without disrupting metrics ingestion; 4) Make Helm/Terraform provisioning idempotent and upgrade/rollback-friendly for constrained on-prem environments. What changed (summary): - New Terraform module: terraform/modules/observability-diff - exposes an object-bucket (S3/GCS/MinIO) backing store and a small state artifact to record last-applied manifests. - Helm chart updates: charts/grafana/templates/versioned-dashboard-crd.yaml and charts/prometheus/templates/alertgroup-annotation.yaml to include metadata for installer-managed versions. - Installer CLI: bin/installer observability sync --dry-run/--apply which runs a k8s dry-run diff, uploads changed manifests to the artifacts bucket, and creates a versioned manifest pointer. - Upgrade/rollback helper: scripts/obs-rollback.sh that can rehydrate the last-known-good dashboards and reapply via Helm with a controlled canary (N pod subset) and wait-for-stable. - Drift detector controller: k8s/controller/observability-drift-controller (lightweight Go binary) that periodically scans managed namespaces and emits DriftDetected events to the console and an internal metrics endpoint. - CI pipeline: added terraform validate, helm lint, and an e2e scenario (minikube) exercising sync->apply->rollback. - Docs and runbooks: docs/observability/drift-detection.md and runbooks/observability-reconcile.md. Compatibility and safety notes: - The state bucket can be configured to use customer-provided MinIO for on-prem installations; the module supports KMS key id strings for encrypted objects. - The rollback path performs Helm upgrade with --reuse-values and a controlled maxSurge=0 canary so running services aren't restarted en masse. - Dashboard JSONs are scrubbed for cluster-specific IDs and timestamp fields prior to versioning to reduce false positives. - For GDPR/audit customers we optionalize dashboard uploads (opt-in via main installer variables). Testing and validation: - Unit: Go controller unit tests and Terraform module unit checks added. - Integration: e2e test simulates a manual dashboard edit in-cluster, runs installer observability sync --dry-run to surface drift, then sync --apply to record and push, and finally scripts/obs-rollback.sh to validate reapplication. - CI: terraform validate, helm lint, go test, and a flaky-tolerant e2e job that runs on a separate runner with minikube 1.30. Backwards-compat: Defaults maintain current behavior (installer does not upload dashboards unless observability.versioning.enabled = true). Migration: An opt-in migration step is provided (bin/installer observability migrate --from-manual) that will snapshot current dashboards on first run. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with bucket + IAM instructions - [x] Helm chart changes for dashboard CRD versioning - [x] Controller binary + unit tests - [x] Installer CLI commands and docs - [x] Rollback script and canary logic - [x] E2E tests and CI integration Related: builds on discussion in ENG-4421 and the SRE runbook from SRE-208. Not included: SIEM forwarding (separate follow-up to wire syslog/CEF).
